references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.155 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1374 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.492

arabic_text: وَعَنَهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ : «صَلاَةَ ٱلْكُسُوفِ إِذَا فَرَغْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْجَلِيَ فَأَعِدْ».
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “If you complete the eclipse prayer (salat
al-kusuf) before the eclipse clears, then repeat it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.156 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1371

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ
عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالاَ: سَألْنَا أُبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ ٱلْكُسُوفِ كَمْ رَكْعَةً هِيَ
وَكَيْفَ نُصَلَّيهَا فَقَالَ «هِيَ عَشْرُ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ أَرْبَعُ سَجَدَاتٍ تَفْتَتِحُ الصَّلاةَ بِتَكْبِيرَةٍ وَ تَرْكَعُ بِتَكْبِيرَةٍ وَ تَرْفَعُ رَأْسَكَ
بِتَكْبِيرَةِ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْخَامِسَةِ الَّتِي تَسْجُدُ فِيهَا فَتَقُولُ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ وَ تَقْنُتُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَبْلَ الرُكُوعِ وَ
تُطَوِّلُ الْقُنُوتَ وَ الرُّكُوعَ عَلَى قَدْرِ ٱلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ الرُكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْجَلِيَ فَاقْعُذْ وَ أُذْعُ اللَّهَ حَتَّى
يَنجَلِيَ فَإِنْ تَجَلَّى قَبْلَ أَنْ تَفْرُغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِكَ فَأْتِمَ مَا بَقِيَ تَجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهَا فَقَالَ «إِنْ
قَرَأْتَ سُورَةً فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ فَاقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ فَإِنْ نَقَصْتَ مِنَ السُّورَةِ شَيْئاً فَاقْرَأُ مِنْ حَيْثُ نَقَصْتَ وَ لا تَقْرَأ
فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ » قَالَ «وَكَانَ يَسْتَجِبُ فِيهَا أَنْ يُقْرَأَ بِالْكَهْفِ وَ الْحِجْرِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ إِمَاماً يَشُقُ عَلَى مَنْ خَلْفَهُ فَإِنٍ
اِسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَكُونَ صَلَاَتُكَ بَارِزاً لا يُجِنُكَ بَيْتٌ فَافْعَلْ وَ صَلَاَةُ كُسُوفِ الشَّمْسِ أَطْوَلُ مِنْ صَلَاةٍ كُسُوفِ الْقَمَرِ وَ
هُمَا سَوَاءً فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ وَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn
Shadhan all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
We asked Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the eclipse prayer (salat al-kusuf),
about how many rak’ahs it has and how we should perform it.
Imam {a.s} said: “It is ten rak’ahs and four prostrations.
You begin the prayer with a takbir, and you bow with a takbir, and you raise your head
with a takbir except in the fifth rak’ah in which you go into prostration;
there you say: ‘SamiAllahu liman hamidah’ (‘Allah {SWT} hears one who praises Him {AZJ}’).
You perform qunut in every two rak’ahs before bowing, and you lengthen the qunut
and the bowing in proportion to the length of the recitation and the bowing.
If you finish before the eclipse has cleared, then sit and supplicate to Allah {SWT} until it
clears. And if the eclipse clears before you have finished your prayer, then complete
whatever remains of your prayer. You recite aloud in this prayer.”
He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘How is the recitation in it?’”
Imam {a.s} said: “If you recite a surah in every rak’ah, then recite ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah
Al Fatihah). But if you shorten the surah and stop before completing it, then continue
from where you left off, and do not repeat Surah al-Fatihah.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And it was recommended in it to recite Surah al-Kahf and Surah al-Hijr
unless the person is leading prayer (as an imam), in which case it may be difficult for
those praying behind him.
So if you are able to perform your prayer in an open space where no house covers you,
then do so.
And the eclipse prayer for the sun is longer than the eclipse prayer for the moon
although they are equal in recitation, bowing, and prostration.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.463 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.156 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1373 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.494

arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ :
«إِذَا اِنْكَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ وَ لَمْ تَعْلَمْ بِهِ حَتَّى أَصْبَحْتَ ثُمَّ بَلَعَكَ فَإِنْ كَانَ اِحْتَرَقَ كُلُّهُ فَعَلَيْكَ الْقَضَاءُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ اِحْتَرَقَ
كُلْهُ فَلا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْكَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Hariz, who said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “If the moon is eclipsed and you were
unaware of it until morning, and then it reaches you (you learn about it), then if the
entire moon had been darkened (ihtaraqa kulluhu), you are obligated to make up the
prayer (qada). But if it had not been completely darkened, then there is no obligation
upon you to make it up.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.157 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1380 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.500

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا اِنْكَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ فَاسْتَيْقَظَ
الرَّجُلُ فَكَسِلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فَلْيَعْتَسِلْ مِنْ غَدِ وَ لَيَقْضِ الصَّلاةَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَيْقِظْ وَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِاتْكِسَافِ الْقَمَرِ فَلَيْسَ
عَلَيْهِ إِلَّ ٱلْقَضَاءُ بِغَيْرٍ غُسْلٍ».
قال محمد بن الحسن : والذي رواه:
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad, from Hariz, from someone who informed him, from Abu Abdillah {a.s},
peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If the moon is eclipsed and a man wakes up but feels lazy to
perform the prayer, then let him perform ghusl the next day and make up the prayer.
But if he did not wake up and was unaware of the lunar eclipse, then he is only required
to make up the prayer, without ghusl.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: “And the one who narrated it is:”
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.1 p.117 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.157 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.453 • Al- Wafi, Vol.6 p.382 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1380 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.336 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.500

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ - عَنْ صَلَاَةِ الْكُسُوفِ
نَقْضِي إِذَا فَاتَثْنَا قَالَ «لَيْسَ فِيهَا قَضَاءُ».
وقد كان في ايدينا انها تقضى. فالمراد بهذا الخبر انه إذا لم يحترق القرص كله واما مع احتراقه كله فلا بد من القضاء
حسب ما قدمناه ويزيده بيانا ما رواه :
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the eclipse prayer, do we make it
up if we miss it?
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no make-up (qadah) for it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
And it was in our hands (it was known to us) that it is to be made up. So, the meaning
of this report is that it applies when the entire disc (of the sun or moon) was not
completely darkened. But if it was entirely darkened, then making it up is necessary,
as we have already stated. And this is further clarified by what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.157 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.453 • Al-Wafi, Vol.9 p.1380 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.501

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَ قَالَ: «إِذَا اِنْكَسَفَتِ الشَّمْسُ
كُلِّهَا وَ اِحْتَرَقَتْ وَ لَمْ تَعْلَمْ وَ عَلِمْتَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَعَلَيْكَ ٱلْقَضَاءُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَحْتَرِقُ كُلَّهَا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاء».
فهذا الخبر والذي قدمناه من رواية حريز جاءا مفصلين وحديث ان لا قضاء عليه مجمل والحكم بالمفصل على المجمل
أولى.
١٠_ باب أحكام فوائت الصلاة
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : ومن فاتته صلاة بخروج وقتها قضاها كما فاتته ولم يؤخرها إلا ان يمنع منه تضيق وقت فرض ثان
عليه. قد بينا فيما مضى ان من فاتته صلاة فليصلها أي وقت ذكرها ما لم يخف فوت صلاة وفيه كفاية :
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu
Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If the sun is fully eclipsed and completely darkened, and you
were unaware of it but came to know afterward, then you are obligated to make it up
(qadah). But if it was not fully darkened, then there is no obligation upon you to make
it up.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
Thus, this report, along with the one we presented earlier from the narration of Hariz,
has come in detailed form, whereas the hadith stating that there is no obligation to
make it up is general. And applying the detailed (mufassal) report to explain the
general (mujmal) one is preferable.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “Whoever misses a
prayer by its time passing, must make it up just as it was missed, and he should not
delay it unless he is prevented by the narrowness of the time of another obligatory
prayer that has become due upon him.”
We have already explained earlier that whoever misses a prayer should perform it
whenever he remembers it, as long as he does not fear missing another obligatory
prayer, and that is sufficient. What further clarifies this is what was narrated:

arabic_text:
مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَادٍ عَنْ
حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرِ عَ قَالَ: «إِذَا نَسِيتَ صَلاةً أَوْ صَلّيْتَهَا بِغَيْرِ وُضُوء وَ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ صَلَوَاتُ فَابْدَأْ
بِأَوَّلِهِنَّ فَأَذِّنْ لَهَا وَ أَقِمْ ثُمَّ صَلَّهَا ثُمَّ صَلِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا بِإِقَامَةٍ إِقَامَةٍ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةِ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ عَ «وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ
قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ الظُهْرَ وَ قَدْ فَاتَثكَ ٱلْغَدَاةُ فَذَكَرْتَهَا فَصَلَّ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ ذَكَرْتَهَا وَ لَوْ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ وَ مَتَى مَا ذَكَزْتَ صَلاَةً
فَاتَثكَ صَلَّيْتَهَا» وَ قَالَ «إِنْ نَسِيتَ الظُّهرَ حَتَّى صَلِّيْتَ الْعَصْرَ فَذَكَرْتَهَا وَ أَنْتَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ أَوْ بَعْدَ فَرَاعِكَ فَانُوِهَا
الْأُولَى ثُمَّ صَلِّ الْعَصْرَ فَإِنَّهَا هِيَ أَرْبَعُ صَلِّيْتَهَا مَكَانَ أَرْبَعِ وَ إِنْ ذَكَزْتَ أَنَّكَ لَمْ تُصَلِّ الْأُولَى وَ أَنْتَ فِي صَلَاَةِ الْعَصْرِ
وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ مِنْهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَصَلّ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْبَاقِيَتَيْنِ وَ قُمْ فَصَلَ الْعَصْرَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ ذَكَرْتَ أَنَّكَ لَمْ تُصَلَّ الْعَصْرَ
حَتَّى دَخَلَ وَقْتُ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَ لَمْ تَخَفْ فَوْتَهَا فَصَلَ الْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ صَلَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَقُمْ فَصَلَّ
اَلْعَصْرَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتَ الْعَصْرَ فَانْوِهَا الْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ ثُمَّ صَلِّ الْمَغْرِبَ وَ إِنْ
كُنْتَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ وَ نَسِيتَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَقُمْ فَصَلَ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ ذَكَرْتَهَا وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتَ مِنَ الْعِشَاءِ
الْآخِرَةِ رَكْعَتَيْنٍ أَوْ قُمْتَ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ فَانْوِهَا الْمَغْرِبَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمْ ثُمَّ قُمْ فَصَلَّ الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ نَسِيتَ
اَلْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ حَتَّى صَلَّيْتَ الْفَجْرَ فَصَلِّ الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ ذَكَرْتَهَا وَ أَنْتَ فِي رَكْعَةٍ أَوْ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ
اَلْغَدَاةِ فَانْوِهَا الْعِشَاءَ ثُمّ قُمْ فَصَلَّ الْغَدَاةَ وَ أَذِّنْ وَ أَقِمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ الْمَغْرِبُ وَ الْعِشَاءُ قَدْ فَاتَتَاكَ جَمِيعا فَابْدَأُ بِهِمَا
قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ ٱلْغَدَاةَ إِبْدَأُ بِالْمَعْرِبِ ثُمَّ ٱلْعِشَاءِ وَ إِنْ خَشِيتَ أَنْ تَفُوتَكَ الْغَدَاةُ إنْ بَدَأْتَ بِهِمَا فَابْدَأُ بِالْمَعْرِبِ ثُمَّ
بِالْغَدَاةِ ثُمَّ صَلِّ الْعِشَاءَ وَ إِنْ خَشِيتَ أَنْ تَفُوتَكَ صَلاَةُ الْغَدَاةِ إِنْ بَدَأْتَ بِالْمَغْرِبِ فَصَلّ الْغَدَاةَ ثُمَّ صَلِّ الْمَغْرِبَ وَ
الْعِشَاءَ اِبْدَأُ بِأَوَّلِهِمَا لِأَنَّهُمَا جَمِيعاً قَضَاءُ أَيَّهُمَا ذَكَزْتَ فَلا تُصَلَّهِمَا إِلاَّا بَعْدَ شُعَاعِ الشَّمْسِ » قَالَ قُلْتُ لِمَ ذَاكَ قَالَ
«لِأَنَّكَ لَسْتَ تَخَافُ فَوْتَهُ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn
Shadhan, all from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “If you forget a prayer or you performed it without ablution, and
there are missed prayers upon you, then begin with the first of them. Call the adhan
for it and the iqamah, then pray it. After that, pray the one that follows it, with an
iqamah, an iqamah for each prayer.”
He (Zurarah) said: “And Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said:
‘And if you had already performed Dhuhr while the morning prayer had passed you,
then you remembered it, then pray it at whatever hour you remember it, even after Asr.
And whenever you remember a prayer that has passed you, then pray it.”
And Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “If you forget the Dhuhr prayer until you have prayed the
Asr prayer, then you remember it while you are in the prayer or after you have finished,
then intend that (what you just prayed) be the first (Dhuhr), and then pray the Asr.
For it is four (rak’ahs) that you have prayed in place of four.
And if you remember that you did not pray the first (Dhuhr) while you are in the Asr
prayer, and you have already prayed two rak’ahs of it, then complete the remaining
two rak’ahs (as Dhuhr), and then stand and pray the Asr.
And if you remember that you did not pray Asr, until the time of Maghrib has entered,
and you do not fear missing it, then pray the Asr and then pray the Maghrib.
And if you had already prayed the Maghrib, then stand and pray the Asr. And if you had
already prayed two rak’ahs of Maghrib, then you remembered Asr, then intend it as
Asr, then give salam, then pray Maghrib.
And if you had prayed the last Isha prayer and had forgotten Maghrib, then stand and
pray Maghrib. And if you remembered it and you had already prayed two rak’ahs of the
last Isha or you had stood up for the third, then intend it as Maghrib, then give salam,
then stand and pray the last Isha.
And if you had forgotten the last Isha prayer until you prayed the fajr, then pray the last
Isha prayer. And if you remembered it while you were in a rak’ah or in the second
(rak’ah) of the morning prayer, then intend it as Isha, then stand and pray the morning
prayer. Call the adhan and the iqamah.
And if both Maghrib and Isha have passed you, then begin with them before you pray
the morning prayer, then begin with Maghrib, and then Isha.
And if you fear that the morning prayer will be missed if you begin with them, then begin
with Maghrib, then the morning prayer, then pray Isha.
And if you fear that the morning prayer will be missed if you begin with Maghrib, then
pray the morning prayer, then pray Maghrib and Isha.
Begin with whichever of the two came first, because both of them are qadha (make-
up prayers). Whichever of them you remember, do not pray them except after the
sunrise rays appear.”
He (Zurarah) said: “I asked, ‘Why is that?’”
Imam {a.s} said: “Because you do not fear missing it.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.291 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.158 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1013 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.290

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ : أَنَّهُ
سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجْلٍ صَلَّى بِغَيْرِ طَهُورٍ أَوْ نَسِيَ صَلاَةً لَمْ يُصَلَّهَا أَوْ نَامَ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ «يَقْضِيهَا إِذَا ذَكَرَهَا فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ
ذَكَرَهَا مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ فَإِذَا دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ وَ لَمْ يُتِمَّ مَا قَدْ فَاتَهُ فَلْيَقْضٍ مَا لَمْ يَتَخَوَّف أَنْ يَذْهَبَ وَقْتُ هَذِهِ
الصَّلَاةِ آَلَّتِي قَدْ حَضَرَتْ وَ هَذِهِ أَحَقُ فَلْيَقْضِهَا فَإِذَا قَضَاهَا فَلْيُصَلّ مَا قَدْ فَانَهُ مِمَّا قَدْ مَضَى وَ لا يَتَطَوَّعُ بِرَكْعَةٍ
حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ ٱلْفَرِيضَةَ كُلَّهَا».
english_text:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah,
from Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} was asked about a man who prayed without purification, or who
forgot a prayer and did not perform it, or who slept through it.
Imam {a.s} said: “He must make it up when he remembers it, at whatever hour he
remembers it whether by night or by day.
And if the time of (another) prayer enters while he has not yet completed what has
passed him, then let him make up (the missed prayer), so long as he does not fear that
the time of the present prayer will pass.
And this (present prayer) has more right, so let him perform it.
Then once he has prayed it, let him pray what had previously passed him of missed
prayers. And he should not perform any supererogatory (nafl) rak’ah until he has made
up all of the obligatory prayers.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.292 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.172 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.266 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.159 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.286 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1011 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.256

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيَّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ ٱلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ
اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلْى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَ هُوَ جُنُبُ الْيَوْمَ وَ الْيَوْمَيْنِ وَ الثَّلَاَثَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ «يَتَطَهَّرُ وَ
يُؤَذَّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ فِي أَوْلِهِنَّ ثُمّ يُصَلِّي وَ يُقِيمُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ فَيْصَلِّي بِغَيْرِ أَذَانِ حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ صَلاَتَهُ».
قال الشيخ رحمه الله : ومن فاتته صلاة الجمعة صلاها اربعا. يدل على ذلك ما رواه :
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Hariz from Muhammad
ibn Muslim. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who prayed the prayers
while he was in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), for a day or two or three, then
remembered afterward.
Imam {a.s} said: “He must perform purification, then call the adhan and give the iqamah
for the first of them (meaning prayers performed whilst junub), then pray.
After that, he gives the iqamah for each subsequent prayer and prays without
(repeating) the adhan, until he completes all of his missed prayers.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “Whoever misses the
Friday prayer (Salat Al Jumu'ah) should perform it as four (rak’ahs)”.
This is supported by what has been narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.159 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1008 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.254

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثَمَانَ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَمَّنْ لَمْ يُذْرِكِ الْخُطِبَةَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَإِنْ فَاتَتْهُ الصَّلاَةُ فَلَمْ يُدْرِكُهَا
فَلْيُصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً» وَ قَالَ «إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ ٱلْإِمَامَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ ٱلْأَخِيرَةَ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتَ ٱلصَّلاَةَ فَإِنْ أَنْتَ أَدْرَكْتَهُ بَعْدَ مَا رَكَعَ
فَهِيَ الظُهْرُ أَرْبَعْ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman
from al-Halabi. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about someone who did not catch the
sermon on the day of Jumu’ah (Friday).
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray two rak’ahs. But if he missed the prayer and did not
catch it, then let him pray four (rak’ahs).”
And Imam {a.s} said: “If you catch the imam (of prayer) before he bows in the final
(rak’ah), then you have caught the prayer. But if you catch him after he has bowed,
then (pray) it as Dhuhr, (which is) four (rak’ahs).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.427 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.160 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.243 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.421 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1159 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.345

arabic_text:
مُحَمّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يُوسُفَ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْعَرْزَمِيَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ
جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيّ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ أَدْرَكَ الإِمَامَ يَوْمَ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ وَ هُوَ يَتَشَهَدُ فَلْيُصَلَ أَرْبَعاً وَ
مَنْ أَدْرَكَ رَكْعَةً فَلْيُضِفُ إِلَيْهَا أُخْرَى يَجْهَرُ فِيهَا».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Yusuf ibn al-Harith from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzami
from his father Abd al-Rahman from Ja’far from his father from Jabir from Imam Ali {a.s}, peace be upon him.
He said:
Imam Ali {a.s} said: “Whoever catches the imam (of prayer) on the day of Friday while he
is reciting the tashahhud, let him pray four (rak’ahs).
And whoever catches one rak’ah, let him add to it another, in which he recites aloud.”
source: Amir al-Mu’minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Murtadha {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.160 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1160 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.7 p.347

arabic_text:
وَ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَ النَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «الْجُمُعَةُ لا
تَكُونُ إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَدْرَكَ الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ».
فمحمول على انه لا يكون له ثواب من ادرك الخطبتين دون ان تجب عليه اعادة اربع ركعات.
english_text:
And what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah and al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah
{a.s}, peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Friday (prayer) is not valid except for the one who catches
both sermons.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So it is to be understood as meaning that the one who catches both sermons receives
the reward (of Jumu’ah), without it being obligatory upon him to repeat (the prayer as)
four rak’ahs.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.160

arabic_text:
أَلاَتَرَى إِلَى مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ:
«مَنْ أَدْرَكَ رَكْعَةً فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ الْجُمُعَةَ».
فصرح في هذا الخبر أن من ادرك ركعة فقد ادرك الجمعة فلو لم يكن المراد بالخبر الاول ما ذكرناه لتناقضا وهذا فاسد.
english_text:
Do you not see what was narrated by al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik,
He said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever catches one rak’ah has caught
the Friday (prayer).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So, it is explicitly stated in this narration that whoever catches one rak’ah has caught
the Friday (prayer). Therefore, if the meaning of the first narration were not what we
have explained, the two narrations would contradict one another and that is invalid.
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.161

arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ :
عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى فِي جَمَاعَةٍ يَوْمَ جُمُعَةٍ فَلَمَّا رَكَعَ الْإِمَامُ رَكَعَ وَ الْجَأَهُ النَّاسُ إِلَى جِدَارٍ أَوْ أُسْطُوَانَةٍ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى
الرُّكُوعِ وَلَاَ السِّجُودِ حَتَّى رَفَعَ الْقَوْمُ رُءُوسَهُمْ أَيَرْكَعُ ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَلْحَقُ بِالصَّفِّ وَ قَدْ قَامَ الْقَوْمُ أَوْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ
قَالَ «يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّفَّ وَ لا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : وان نسي الحاضر صلاة فذكرها بعد خروج وقتها وهو مسافر قضاها في سفره على التمام.
english_text:
Sa’ad from Ali ibn Ismail from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu al-Hasan {a.s},
peace be upon him:
Imam al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a man who prayed in congregation on the day of
Friday, and when the imam (of prayer) bowed, he bowed as well, but the people
pushed him toward a wall or a pillar, so he was unable to bow or prostrate until the
people had raised their heads. Should he (then) bow and prostrate and catch up with
the row, while the people have already stood up, or what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: “He should prostrate, then stand in the row, and there is no problem in
that.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And if someone who
is a resident forgets a prayer and remembers it after its time has passed, while he is
traveling, he must make it up during his travel in full (as four rak’ahs).”
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.161 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1274

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ الْوَشَاءِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا زَالَتِ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَ أَنْتَ فِي الْمِصْرِ وَ أَنْتَ تُرِيدُ ٱلسَّفَرَ فَأَتِمَ فَإِذَا خَرَجْتَ بَعْدَ ٱلزَّوَالِ قَصِّرِ الْعَصْرَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali
al-Washsha. He said:
I heard Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “If the sun has passed the zenith
while you are still in the city and you intend to travel, then complete (the Dhuhr prayer
in full). But if you depart after the zenith, then shorten the Asr prayer.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.434 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.161 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.224 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.240 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.144 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.516

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ فَرْقَدٍ عَنْ بَشِيرِ النِّبَالِ قَالَ: خَرَجْتُ
مَعَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا الشَّجَرَةَ فَقَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «يَا نَبَّالُ » قُلْتُ لَبَّيْكَ قَالَ
«إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذَا الْعَسْكَرِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ أَرْبَعاً غَيْرِي وَ غَيْرِكَ وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ
نَخْرُجَ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وان نسي المسافر صلاة فذكرها بعد تقضي وقتها وهو حاضر قضاها على التقصير.
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Dawud ibn
Farqad from Bashir al-Nabbal. He said:
I went out with Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, until we reached al-Shajarah.
Then Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me: “O Nabbal!”
I said: “At your service.”
Imam {a.s} said: “It is not obligatory upon anyone in this entire camp to pray four
(rak’ahs) except me and you, and that is because the time of the prayer entered before
we had departed.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And if a traveller
forgets a prayer and remembers it after its time has passed while he is (now) a
resident, he must make it up in shortened form.”
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.434 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.161 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.224 • Al- Istibsar, Vol.1 p.240 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.144 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.515 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.48

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلْ فَاتَثَهُ صَلاَةٌ مِنْ
صَلاَةِ السَّفَرِ فَذَكَرَهَا فِي الْحَضَرِ فَقَالَ «يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ كَمَا فَاتَهُ إِنْ كَانَتْ صَلاَةَ السَّفَرِ أَدّاهَا فِي الْحَضَرِ مِثلَهَا وَ
إِنْ كَانَتْ صَلاَةَ الْحَضَرِ فَلْيَقْضٍ فِي السَّفَرِ صَلاَةَ الْحَضَرِ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah. He said:
I said to Imam {a.s}: “A man misses a prayer while he is on a journey, then remembers it
while in residence.”
Imam {a.s} said: “He must make up what he missed in the same manner as it was
missed. If it was a prayer of travel, he performs it in residence as it was (shortened).
And if it was a prayer of residence, then let him make it up during travel as a prayer of
residence.”
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.435 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.162 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.163 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1009 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.268

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ النَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ
رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ وَ هُوَ فِي السَّفَرِ فَأَخَرَ الصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى قَدِمَ فَهُوَ يُرِيدُ يُصَلِّيهَا إِذَا قَدِمَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فَنَسِيَ جِينَ
قَدِمَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ أَنْ يُصَلَّيَهَا حَتَّى ذَهَبَ وَقْتُهَا قَالَ «يُصَلَّيهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ صَلاَةَ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ لِأَنَ ٱلْوَقْتَ دَخَلَ وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ
كَانَ يَنبَغِي لَهُ أُنْ يُصَلَّيَ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far {a.s} :
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} was asked about a man upon whom the time of prayer entered while
he was on a journey, and he delayed the prayer until he arrived (at his destination),
intending to pray it when he reached his family. Then, when he arrived, he forgot to
pray it until its time had passed.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray it as two rak’ahs, as the prayer of a traveller, because
the time entered while he was traveling. It would have been appropriate for him to pray
at that time.”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.13 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.162 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.225 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1009 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.268 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.513 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.51

arabic_text:
فَأَمَا مَا رَوَاهُ ٱلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعِيصِ بْنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ
عَنِ الرَّجْلِ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ وَقْتُ الصَّلاَةِ فِي السَّفَرِ ثُمَّ يَدْخُلُ بَيْتَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلَّيَهَا قَالَ «يُصَلِّيهَا أَرْبَعاً» وَ قَالَ «لا
يَزَالُ يُقَصَّرُ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ بَيْتَهُ».
فان هذه الرواية محمولة على انه إذا دخل وكان الوقت باقيا يجب عليه التمام فاما بعد مضي الوقت لا يجب عليه القضاء
إلا حسب ما فاتته، وكذلك إذا خرج إلى السفر وكان الوقت باقيا وجب عليه التقصير. والذي يدل على ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Is ibn al-Qasim, he said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man upon whom the time of
prayer enters while he is traveling, then he enters his house before having prayed it.
He said: “He must pray it as four (rak’ahs).”
And Imam {a.s} said: “He continues to shorten (the prayer) until he enters his house.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
This narration is to be understood as referring to the case when he enters (his home)
and the time (for the prayer) still remains then it becomes obligatory upon him to
perform it in full. But as for when the time has passed, then it is not obligatory upon
him to make it up except in the manner it was missed.
Likewise, if he set out for travel while the time still remained, then shortening (the
prayer) is obligatory upon him. And what indicates this is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.162 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.148 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.513

arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ
يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ وَ أَنَا فِي السَّفَرِ فَلاَ أصَلِّي حَتَّى أَدْخَلَ أَهْلِي قَالَ «صَلِّ وَ أَتِمّ الصَّلاةَ» قُلْتُ فَدَخَلَ وَقْتُ
الصَّلَاةِ وَأَنَا فِي أَهْلِي أَرِيدُ السَّفَرَ فَلاَ أُصَلِّي حَتَّى أَخْرُجَ قَالَ «صَلِّ وَ قَصِّرْ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَقَدْ وَ اللّهِ خَالَفْتَ رَسُولَ
اللَّه صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ».
فان قال قائل : لم قلتم انه أذا كان الوقت باقيا بعد دخوله من السفر يجب عليه التمام وكذلك فيمن خرج إلى السفر ان
كان الوقت باقيا يقصر وليس في الخبر ذلك بل هو مطلق ان من خرج إلى السفر بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التقصير،
وكذلك من دخل من السفر يجب عليه التمام وليس فيه اعتبار بقية الوقت؟!!. قلنا : انما اعتبرنا بقية الوقت لئلا تتناقض
الاخبار لانا قد قدمنا أحاديث في ان من خرج إلى السفر بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التمام، وكذلك ان من قدم من السفر
يجب عليه التقصير، وجاء هذا الخبر أن من خرج إلى السفر بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التقصير ، ومن قدم من السفر
بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التمام، احتجنا إلى ان نجمع بين هذه الاخبار فحملنا كل خبر ورد بانه من خرج إلى السفر
بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التمام على ان المراد به بعد تقضي الوقت ، وكذلك فيمن قدم من السفر ، وكل خبر ورد بانه
من خرج إلى السفر بعد دخول الوقت يجب عليه التقصير على انه أذا كان الوقت باقيا وكذلك في القادم من سفر ، لئلا
تتناقض الاخبار، والذى يبين ما ذكرناه خبر حريز المتقدم ذكره، قال قلت له : رجل فاتته صلاة من صلاة السفر فذكرها
في الحضر فقال : يقضي ما فاته كما فاته ان كانت صلاة السفر اداها في الحضر مثلها ، وان كانت صلاة الحضر فليقض
في السفر صلاة الحضر ، فكان هذا الخبر مبينا للاخبار كلها لانه قال : ومن فاتته صلاة فليقضها كما فاتته. ومن قدم من
السفر والوقت باق لم يكن قد فاتته الصلاة ، وكذلك من خرج إلى السفر والوقت باق لم يكن قد فاتته الصلاة ، والذي يبين
ما ذكرناه ايضا ما رواه:
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ismail ibn Jabir. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “The time of prayer enters upon me while
I am traveling, but I do not pray until I enter (the home of) my family.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Pray and complete the prayer (in full).”
I asked: “What if the time of prayer enters upon me, while I am with my family, and I
intend to travel, so I do not pray until I depart?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Pray and shorten the prayer.
And if you do not do so, then by Allah {SWT}, you have opposed the Messenger of Allah
{SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
If someone were to say: ‘Why do you say that if the time still remains after one returns
from travel, it becomes obligatory upon him to perform the prayer in full, and likewise
for the one who sets out for travel if the time still remains, he must shorten the prayer?
Whereas the report is unrestricted and simply states that whoever sets out for travel
after the time has entered must shorten (the prayer), and likewise, whoever returns
from travel must complete it. There is no mention in the report of considering whether
the time remains?!
We say: ‘We considered the remaining time so that the reports do not contradict one
another because we have already presented narrations stating that whoever departs
for travel after the entry of the prayer time must perform it in full.
And likewise, (there are narrations stating) that one who returns from travel must
shorten (the prayer).
And then came this report stating that whoever sets out for travel after the entry of the
prayer time must shorten (the prayer), and that whoever returns from travel after the
entry of the prayer time must complete it.
Therefore, we were compelled to reconcile these reports.
So we interpreted every narration that states; whoever sets out for travel after the entry
of time must perform it in full as referring to when the time has already passed.
And likewise, in the case of one who returns from travel.
And every narration that states; whoever sets out for travel after the entry of time must
shorten (the prayer) we interpreted it to mean, ‘if the time still remains’.
And the same applies to one who returns from travel.
So that the reports do not contradict one another. And what clarifies what we have
mentioned is the narration of Hariz that was cited earlier.
He (Hariz) said: “I said to Imam {a.s},
‘A man misses a prayer while on a journey, then remembers it while in residence’.”
Imam {a.s} said:
“He must make up what he missed in the same manner as it was missed.
If it was a prayer of travel, he performs it in residence in the same manner.
And if it was a prayer of residence, then let him make it up while traveling as a prayer
of residence.”
So this narration serves as an explanation for all the reports, because Imam {a.s} said:
“Whoever misses a prayer, let him make it up as it was missed.”
And the one who returns from travel while the time still remains has not yet missed the
prayer, and likewise, the one who departs for travel while the time still remains has not
yet missed the prayer.
And what also clarifies what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.443 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.13 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.163 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.222 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.240 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.111 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.146 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.512 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.46

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيْوبَ عَنِ الْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ : فِي الرّجُلِ يَقْدَمُ مِنَ الْغَيْبَةِ فَيَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ وَقْتُ الصَّلاةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ ٱلْوَقْتُ
فَلْيَدْخُلْ فَلْيُتِمَّ وَ إِنْ كَانَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ الْوَقْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فَلْيُصَلٌ وَ لَيُقَصِّرْ».
فرغب عليه السلام بهذا الخبر في ان من لم يخف فوت الوقت في تأخير الصلاة حتى يدخل البيت يؤخرها حتى يؤديها
على التمام، فلولا ان فوت الوقت كان مراعى في هذا الباب لم يكن لتقييد الاتمام بهذه الحال معنى. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه
: ولا يؤم المسافر الحاضر ولا الحاضر المسافر، الاولى والافضل ان لا يصلي المسافر خلف المقيم ولا المقيم خلف المسافر
، فان فعلا ذلك تركا الافضل وجازت صلاتهما ، ومتى صلى المسافر خلف المقيم يصلي ركعتين ولينصرف. وإذا صلى
المسافر بالقوم يصلي بهم ركعتين ثم يقدم من يتم الصلاة بهم ولينصرف هو. والذي يدل على ما ذكرناه ما رواه:
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Ala ibn Razin from Muhammad
ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams {a.s}, peace be upon them:
Imam {a.s} was asked concerning a man who returns from a journey and the time of
prayer enters upon him.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he does not fear that the time will end, then let him enter and perform
it in full. But if he fears that the time will expire before he enters, then let him pray and
shorten (the prayer).”
source: Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir {a.s} & Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al- Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So, in this narration, the Imam {a.s}, peace be upon him, encouraged that if one does
not fear the passing of the prayer time when delaying the prayer until he enters his
home, then he should delay it so that he may perform it in full.
If the expiration of the time were not a consideration in this matter, then there would
be no meaning in restricting the performance of the prayer in full to this specific
condition.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A traveller should not
lead a resident in prayer, nor should a resident lead a traveller. The preferable and
better course is that a traveller should not pray behind a resident, nor a resident
behind a traveller. But if they do so, they have only abandoned what is better, and their
prayers are valid. And whenever a traveller prays behind a resident, he should pray two
rak’ahs and then leave. And if a traveller leads a group in prayer, he should lead them
in two rak’ahs, then appoint someone else to complete the prayer with them, and he
himself should leave.”
And what indicates what we have mentioned is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.164 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.146 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.514

arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ الْفَضْلِ
بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ قَالَ: «لا يَوُمُ ٱلْحَضَرِيُ ٱلْمُسَافِرَ وَ لاَ ٱلْمُسَافِرُ الْحَضَرِيَّ فَإِنِ أُبْثُلِيّ
بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَمَّ قَوْما حَاضِرِينَ فَإِذَا أَنَمَّ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَمَ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِيَدِ بَعْضِهمْ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَأَمَّهُمْ وَ إِذَا صَلَّى ٱلْمُسَافِرُ
خَلْفَ قَوْمِ حُضُورِ فَلْيُتِمَ صَلاَتَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُسَلَّمُ وَ إِنْ صَلَّى مَعَهُمُ ٱلظُهْرَ فَلْيَجْعَلِ ٱلْأُولَيَيْنِ ٱلظُهْرَ وَ الْأُخْرَبَيْنِ
الْعصرَ».
english_text:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from
Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “A resident should not lead a traveller in prayer, nor should a
traveller lead a resident.
But if one is put in a situation where this occurs, and he (the traveller) leads a group of
residents in prayer, then when he completes two rak’ahs, he should give salam and
then take the hand of one of them and bring him forward to lead them.
And if a traveller prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as
two rak’ahs and give salam.
And if he prays Dhuhr with them, then let him consider the first two rak’ahs as Dhuhr
and the latter two as Asr.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.164 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.226 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.426 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1258 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.330

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ اللُوْلُوِيِّ عَنِ ٱلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ بْنِ فَضَالٍ عَنْ أَبِي ٱلْمِعْزَى حُمَيْدِ بْنِ ٱلْمُثَنَّى عَنْ عِمْرَانَ
عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ : أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ الْمُسَافِرِ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ مَعَ الْمُقِيمِينَ قَالَ
«فَلْيُصَلّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ لْيُسَلَّمْ وَ لَيَجْعَلِ الْأَخْرَبَيْنِ سُبْحَةً».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu al-Miza
Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Imran from Muhammad ibn Ali:
(Muhammad ibn Ali) asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who
enters into prayer with residents.
Imam {a.s} said: “Let him perform his (own) prayer, then give salam, and make the last
two (rak’ahs) supererogatory (nafila) prayer.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.165 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.227 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.425 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1257 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.330

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثِمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ - عَنِ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ
يُصَلِّي خَلْفَ ٱلْمُقِيمِ قَالَ «يُصَلَّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَمْضِي حَيْثُ شَاءَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays behind a
resident.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray two rak’ahs and then go wherever he wishes.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.165 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.227 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.425 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.329

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو
عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : «لَا يُصَلِّي الْمُسَافِرُ مَعَ الْمُقِيمِ فَإِنْ صَلَّى فَلْيَنْصَرِف فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Husayn ibn Uthman from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Abu
Basir. He said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The traveller should not pray with the
resident. But if he does pray, then let him leave after two rak’ahs.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.165 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.426 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1259 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.329

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ
قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ - عَنِ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ ٱلْإِمَامِ فَيُدْرِكُ مِنَ الصَّلاةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَيُجَزِي ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ
فَقَالَ »نَعَمْ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from
Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays with the imam
(of prayer) and catches two rak’ahs of the prayer. Does that suffice him?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.439 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.165 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1257 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.331

arabic_text:
سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ
مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ٱلنُّعْمَانِ الْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا دَخَلَ الْمُسَافِرُ مَعَ أَقْوَامِ حَاضِرِينَ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ
فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْأُولَى فَلْيَجْعَلِ الْفَرِيضَةَ فِي الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ الْعَضْرُ فَلْيَجْعَلِ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ الْأَجِيرَتَيْنِ
فَرِيضَةٌ».
وفقه هذا الحديث انه انما قال ان كانت الظهر فليجعل الفريضة في الركعتين الاولتين لانه متى فعل ذلك جاز له ان يجعل
الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاة العصر، وإذا كان صلاة العصر انما يجعل الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاته لانه يكره الصلاة بعد صلاة
العصر إلا على جهة القضاء، ومن صلى على ما قلناه لم يبق عليه شئ ويحتسب به من النوافل. قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : ولا
يؤم المتيمم المتوضئين ولا يؤم المتوضى ، المتيممين. وهذه المسألة مثل الاولى في ان الاولى ان لا يؤم المتيمم
المتوضئين ولو فعل ذلك لم يكن بذلك مبطلا لصلاته لكنه يكون قد ترك الافضل، فاما الذي يدل على كراهة ذلك ما رواه:
english_text:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from
Abdillah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Numan al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He
said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “If a traveller joins a group of residents in their prayer, then if it
is the first (Dhuhr) prayer, let him make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs.
And if it is the Asr prayer, let him make the first two (rak’ahs) supererogatory and the
last two obligatory.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The understanding of this hadith is that Imam {a.s} only said, ‘If it is Dhuhr, let him make
the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs,’ because when he does so, it becomes
permissible for him to make the last two rak’ahs into the Asr prayer.
And when it is the Asr prayer, he makes the last two rak’ahs his prayer, because it is
disliked to pray after Asr except as make-up (qadah).
So, whoever prays as we have described, nothing remains upon him, and the (extra)
rak’ahs are counted for him among the supererogatory (nafl) prayers.
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A person performing
tayammum should not lead those who have performed wudu, and likewise, one who
has performed wudu should not lead those performing tayammum.”
This matter is similar to the previous one, in that it is preferable that a person
performing tayammum not lead those who have performed wudu.
But if he does so, his prayer is not invalidated by that; rather, he has merely abandoned
what is more virtuous.”
As for what indicates the dislike (karahah) of that, it is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.165 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.226 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1259 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.329

arabic_text:
أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ صُهَيْبٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ
يَقُولُ: «لا يُصَلِّي الْمُتَيَمَّمُ بِقَوْمِ مُتَوَضِّئِينَ».
english_text:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abbad ibn Suhayb. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, say: “A person performing tayammum
should not lead a group who have performed wudu.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.166 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1177 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.328

arabic_text:
وَرَوَى مُحَمّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِبِهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ السَّكُونِيّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «لا يَؤُمُّ صَاحِبُ التَّيَمُمِ ٱلْمُتَوَضَّئِينَ وَ لا يَؤْمُ صَاحِبُ ٱلْفَالِجِ الْأَصِحَاءَ».
فان قيل : ظاهر هذين الخبرين انه لا يجوز ان يؤم المتيمم المتوضئين على وجه فلم حملتم على الكراهة دون الحضر!!؟.
قلنا : انما فعلنا ذلك لورود اخبار كثيرة تتضمن جواز ذلك فاحتجنا ان نجمع بينها فمن ذلك ما رواه :
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-
Sakuni from Imam Ja’far {a.s}, from his father Imam al-Baqir {a.s}, peace be upon them, said:
Imam al-Baqir {a.s} said: “A person who performs tayammum should not lead those who
have performed wudu, and a person afflicted with paralysis (al-falij) should not lead
those who are healthy.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al- Baqir {a.s}
commentary:
If it is said: ‘The apparent meaning of these two narrations is that it is not permissible
for one performing tayammum, to lead those who have performed wudu at all.
So why did you interpret them as indicating mere dislike (karahah), rather than
prohibition (hurmah)?’
We say: ‘We did so because there are numerous narrations that explicitly indicate the
permissibility of this, so we were compelled to reconcile them.
Among those is what was narrated:’
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.166 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1177 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.328

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيِى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلاَمُ
: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مَاءُ وَ هُوَ إِمَامُ الْقَوْمِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ يَتَيَمَّمُ وَ يَوْمُّهُمْ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah
from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said concerning a man who enters a state of janabah (major ritual
impurity) and has no water, and he is the imam (of prayer) of the people.
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them in prayer.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.544 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.328

arabic_text:
وَمِنْهُ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ
بُكَيْرِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَجْتَبَ ثُمَّ تَيَمَّمَ فَأَمَّنَا وَ نَحْنُ طَهُورٌ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِهِ».
english_text:
And among them is what was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn
ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdillah ibn Bukayr. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s} about a man who entered a state of janabah, then performed
tayammum and led us in prayer while we were in a state of full purity.
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.424 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.327

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمِّدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ وَ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ
قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِمَامُ قَوْمٍ أَصَابَثْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مِنَ ٱلْمَاءِ مَا يَكْفِيهِ لِلْغُسْلِ أَ
يَتَوَضَّا بَعْضُهُمْ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهمْ فَقَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ تَيَمَّمَ ٱلْجُنُبُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جَعَلَ التَّرَابَ طَهُوراً».
english_text:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from
Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj. They said:
I said to Aba Abdillah {a.s}: “An imam (of prayer) of a group, who becomes junub (ritually
impure due to major impurity) during travel, and does not have enough water for ghusl,
should someone among them who has wudu lead them in prayer?”
Imam {a.s} said: “No. Rather, the one in a state of janabah should perform tayammum
and lead them in prayer, for Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Exalted, has made the earth a
purifier.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.66 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.109 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.425 • Al-Wafi, Vol.6 p.543 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.3 p.386 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.327

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ هُوَ جُنْبٌ وَ قَدْ تَيَمَمَ وَ هُمْ عَلَى طَهُورِ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وتقضى الصلاة بالاذان والاقامة إذا فات الانسان ذلك. فقد قدمنا ما يدل على ذلك وبزيده بيانا ما
رواه :
english_text:
And from him, from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I said to Imam {a.s}: “A man led a group in prayer while he was in a state of janabah and
had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of full purification (taharah).”
Imam {a.s} said: “There is no harm in it.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And a missed prayer
is to be made up with adhan and iqamah, if a person missed them.”
We have already presented what indicates this, and what further clarifies it is what
was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.425 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1177 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.327

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ
السَابَاطِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ إِذَا أَعَادَ الصَّلاَةَ هَلْ يُعِيدُ الْأَذَانَ وَ الْإِقَامَةَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : وتقضى فوائت النوافل في كل حال ما لم يكن وقت فريضة أو عند طلوع الشمس أو عند غروبها ،
ويكره قضاء النوافل عند اصفرار الشمس حتى تغيب.
فقد مضى فيما تقدم ما يدل عليه مستوفى ، ويزيد ذلك وضوحا ما رواه:
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amru ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn
Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who repeats a prayer does he also repeat
the adhan and the iqamah?
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah
{SWT} have mercy on him, said: “Missed
supererogatory prayers (nawafil) may be made up at any time, except during the time
of an obligatory prayer, or at sunrise or sunset. And it is disliked to make up nawafil
during the yellowing of the sun until it sets.”
What has preceded contains comprehensive evidence for this, and what further
clarifies it is what was narrated:
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.167 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.609 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.270

arabic_text:
عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيَّ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ «اِقْضِ
مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ النَّهَارِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اللَّيْلِ بِاللَّيْلِ» قُلْتُ أَقْضِي وَثْرَيْنٍ فِي لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ اِقْضٍ
وَثْراً أَبَداً».
english_text:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Fadalah from Muawiyah ibn Ammar. He said:
Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, said to me (Ibn Ammar):
“Make up what you missed of the daytime prayer during the day, and what you missed
of the night prayer during the night.”
I asked: “Should I make up two witr prayers in one night?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, always make up the witr prayer.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.451 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.162 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.168 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.1031 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.276

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَ الْحَسَنِ عَنِ ٱلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «اِقْضِ صَلاَةَ النَّهَارِ أيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ سَوَاءُ».
english_text:
And from him, from al-Hasan from Fadalah and al-Hasan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn
ibn Abi al-Ala from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “Make up the daytime prayer at whatever hour you wish
whether by night or by day all of that is the same.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.173 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.168 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.290 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.358 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.243 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.277 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.71

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبِيبِ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى
أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ تَكُونُ عَلَيَّ الصَّلاةُ النَّافِلَةُ مَتَى أَقْضِيهَا فَكَتَبَ «أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : ولا يجب على المسافر قضاء ما قصر فيه من فريضة ولا نافلة إلا المفروض من الصيام فانه لابد من
قضائه. إذا ثبت بما قدمنا ذكره ان صلاة المسافر من الفرائض. النوافل هو القدر الذي ذكرنا فمتى فعله الانسان لا يلزمه
قضاء ما لم يفرض عليه ولم يندب إليه وهذا القدر كاف في هذا الباب ويؤكد ذلك ايضا ما رواه:
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn
Yahya ibn Habib. He said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, peace be upon him: “I have missed the supererogatory
prayers (nafilah), when should I make them up?”
So Imam al-Ridha {a.s} wrote: “Whenever you wish by night or by day.”
source: Abu al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “A traveller is not
obligated to make up what he shortened from the obligatory prayer or the
supererogatory prayers, except for obligatory fasting, for that must be made up.”
It has been established by what we have mentioned earlier, that the prayer of a
traveller, whether from the obligatory or supererogatory acts, is limited to what we
have specified. So whenever a person performs that amount, he is not required to
make up what was neither obligatory upon him nor recommended to do. And this
much is sufficient on the matter.
What further affirms this is also what was narrated:
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.454 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.272 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.168 • Al- Wafi, Vol.7 p.355 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.240

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونَسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ
عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: «الصَلاَةُ فِي السَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّ
بَعْدَهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لا سَفَرٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ النَّهَارِ وَ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَ اِقْضِهِ».
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّه : والمتمم في السفر ناسيا يعيد إن كان الوقت باقيا وان خرج الوقت فلا اعادة عليه، ومن تعمد التمام
في السفر بعد الحجة عليه في التقصير لم يجزه ذلك ووجب عليه الاعادة.
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-
Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before
them nor after them, except for Maghrib.
For after Maghrib, are four rak’ahs; do not leave them out whether in residence or
travel. And there is no make-up upon you for the daytime prayers, but pray the night
prayer and make it up (if missed).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “And one who
completes (the prayer as four rak’ahs) while traveling, out of forgetfulness, must
repeat the prayer if the time still remains; but if the time has passed, then there is no
repetition upon him. However, whoever deliberately performs the prayer in full while
traveling, after the proof for shortening has been established for him, his prayer is not
valid and he must repeat it.”
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.439 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.2 p.14 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.169 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.119 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.83 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.67

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ ٱلْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا
عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ فَأْتَمَ الصَّلاَةَ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ الْوَقْتُ
قَدْ مَضَى فَلاَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Is
ibn al-Qasim. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who was traveling and
performed the prayer in full.
Imam {a.s} said: “If it is still within the time (of the prayer), then he should repeat it. But
if the time has already passed, then no (he does not need to repeat it).”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.435 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.169 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.967 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.505

arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ عَنْ سُوَيْدِ الْقَلاءِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ يَنْسَى فَيُصَلِّي فِي السَّفَرِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ ذَكَرَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ فَلْيْعِذْ
وَ إنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمُ فَلاَ إعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ».
فهذا الخبر محمول على ضرب من الاستحباب والاول على الوجوب.
١١ - باب صلاة السفينة
قال الشيخ رحمه اللّٰه : وتتوجه إلى القبلة في السفينة وتصلي قائما ان قدرت وإلا جالسا، وإذا دارت السفينة ادرت وجهك
إلى القبلة، فان عدمت معرفة القبلة بعد توجهك بدورانها اجزأك التوجه الاول ودرت معها حيث دارت ، وإذا التبست القبلة
عليك في النوافل أو بعد طلب علاماتها عليك توجهت إلى رأس السفينة فصليت مصعدة ومنحدرة وكيف دارت.
english_text:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Numan from Suwayd al-Qalla from Abu Ayyub from
Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who forgets and prays four rak’ahs while
traveling.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he remembers on the same day, then let him repeat (the prayer). But
if he does not remember until that day has passed, then there is no repetition upon
him.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
commentary:
So this narration is to be understood as indicating a form of recommended
(mustahabb) action, while the first one indicates obligation (wujub).
The Shaykh (Al-Mufid), may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, said: “You must face the
qiblah on a ship and pray standing if you are able; otherwise, (you may pray) sitting.
If the ship turns, you should turn your face toward the qiblah.
But if, after having initially faced it, the ship turns and you are unable to determine the
qiblah due to the movement, then your initial direction suffices, and you continue to
face wherever it turns.
And if the qiblah becomes unclear to you in supererogatory prayers or after seeking its
indications, then you should face the front of the ship and pray while it is ascending or
descending and however it turns.”
-----
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.169 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.225 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.241 • Al- Wafi, Vol.8 p.967 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.506 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol.86 p.54

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يُسْأَلُ
عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي السَّفِينَةِ فَيَقُولُ «إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْثُمْ أَنْ تَخْرُجُوا إِلَى الْجَدَدِ فَاخْرُجُوا وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا فَصَلُوا قِيَاماً وَ
إِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا فَصَلُوا قُعُوداً وَ تَحَرَّوُا الْقِبْلَةَ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, being asked about prayer on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: “If you are able to go out onto dry land, then go out. But if you are not
able, then pray standing, and if you cannot, then pray sitting. And strive to face the
qiblah.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.441 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.170 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.454 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.525 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.323

arabic_text:
اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ الْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةً عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ
فِي السَّفِينَةِ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ إِذَا لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ ٱلْقِيَامُ فِي السَّفِينَةِ وَ لا يُصَلِّي فِي السَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
الشَّطَّ» وَ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي فِي السَّفِينَةِ يُحَوِّلُ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي كَيْفَ مَا دَارَثْ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Ibrahim said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about prayer on a boat.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray while sitting if he is unable to stand in the boat, and he
should not pray in the boat if he is able to reach the shore.”
And Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray in the boat, turning his face towards the qiblah,
then he may continue the prayer however the boat turns.”
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.170 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.455 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.525 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.4 p.321

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِنَّا أُبْثُلِينَا وَ كُنَّا فِي سَفِينَةٍ فَأَمْسَيْنَا
وَ لَمْ نَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَكَانٍ نَخْرُجُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «أَصْحَابُ السَّفِينَةِ لَيْسَ نُصَلِّي يَوْمَنَا مَا دُمْنَا نَطْمَعُ فِي الْخُرُوجِ» فَقَالَ
«إِنَّ أَبِي كَانَ يَقُولُ «تِلْكَ صَلاَةُ نُوحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ» أَوَ مَا تَرْضَى أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ صَلاَةَ نُوحِ » فَقُلْتُ بَلَى جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ
قَالَ «لا يَضِيقَنَ صَدْرُكَ فَإنَّ نُوحاً قَدْ صَلَّى فِي السَّفِينَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَائِماً أَوْ قَاعِداً قَالَ «بَلْ قَائِماً» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي
رُبَّمَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتُ الْقِبْلَةَ فَدَارَتِ السَّفِينَةُ قَالَ «تَحَرَّ الْقِبْلَةَ بِجَهْدِكَ».
english_text:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him: “We were afflicted with a situation, and
we were on a boat, and evening came upon us while we were unable to find a place
where we could disembark.”
So Imam {a.s} said: “The people of the boat do not pray during the day, as long as they
hope to disembark.”
Then Imam {a.s} said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir {a.s}) used to say:
‘That is the prayer of Nuh {a.s}, peace be upon him.’
And are you not pleased to pray the prayer of Nuh {a.s}?”
I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Do not let your heart be constricted, for Nuh {a.s} prayed on the boat.”
I asked: “While standing or sitting?”
Imam {a.s} said: “Rather, (it was whilst) standing.”
I asked: “Sometimes I face the qiblah, then the boat turns.”
Imam {a.s} said: “Strive to face the qiblah with the best of your effort.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al- Baqir {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.170 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.526 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.506

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي السِّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ «يُصَلِّي
قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعِ الْقِيَامَ فَلْيَجْلِسْ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ دَارَتِ السَّفِينَةُ فَلْيَدُرْ مَعَ الْقِبْلَةِ إِنْ قَدَرَ
عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَلْيَثْبُتْ عَلَى مَقَامِهِ وَ لَيَتَحَرَّ الْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِهِ» وَ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي النَّافِلَةَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ
صَدْرِ السَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةِ إِذَا كَبَّرَ ثُمَّ لا يَضُرُّهُ حَيْثُ دَارَتْ).
٨٦٢ 27
english_text:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid.
He (Sulayman) said: “I asked Imam {a.s} about prayer on a boat.”
Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray while standing, and if he is unable to stand, then let
him sit and pray while facing the qiblah.
If the boat turns, then let him turn with the qiblah if he is able to do so, and if he is not
able to do so, then let him remain in his place and strive to face the qiblah with the
best of his effort.”
And Imam {a.s} said: “He should pray the supererogatory prayer facing the front of the
boat, while he is facing the qiblah when he says the takbir, and it does not harm him
wherever the boat turns afterward.”
source: Implicit (Muzmar)
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.171 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.526 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.5 p.506

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ حَمْرَةَ الْغَنَوِيَّ
عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي السَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا كَانَتْ مُحَمَّلَةً تَقِيلَةً إِذَا قُمْتَ فِيهَا لَمْ
تَتَحَرَّك فَصَلّ قَائِما وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ خَفِيفَةً تَكَفَّأ فَصَلٌ قَاعِداً».
١٢ - باب صلاة الخوف
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq
from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} about prayer on a boat.
Imam {a.s} said: “If it is loaded and heavy, such that when you stand in it, it does not
sway, then pray standing. But if it is light and sways, then pray sitting.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.442 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.458 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.171 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.455 • Al-Wafi, Vol.7 p.527

arabic_text:
مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ آللَّهِ
عَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ الْخَوْفِ قَالَ «يَقُومُ ٱلْإِمَامُ وَ يَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ وَ طَائِفَةٌ بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوَّ فَيُصَلِّي
بِهِمُ الْإِمَامُ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ فَيَمْثُلُ قَائِما وَ يُصَلُونَ هُمُ ٱلرَكْعَةَ الثَّانِيَةَ ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ
ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَقَامِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ ٱلْآخَرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ الرَكْعَةَ الثَانِيَةَ
ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ الْإِمَامُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَتصَرِفُونَ بِتَسْلِيمَةِ» قَالَ «وَ فِي ٱلْمَغْرِبِ
مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ يَقُومُ الْإِمَامُ وَ تَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ فَيَمْثَلُ الْإِمَامُ قَائِمَاً وَ
يُصَلُونَ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَتَشَهَدُونَ وَ يُسَلَّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضِ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ
الْآخْرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفٍ أَصْحَابِهِمْ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً يَقْرَأُ فِيهَا ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَقُومُ وَ
يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ».
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
I asked Aba Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about the prayer of fear.
Imam {a.s} said: “The imam (of prayer) stands, and a group from among his companions
comes and stands behind him, while another group positions themselves facing the
enemy. Then the imam (of prayer) leads that group in one rak’ah, then he stands and
they stand with him, and he remains standing while they complete the second rak’ah.
Then they give salam to one another and depart, and they go to take the place of their
companions. Then the others come and stand behind the imam (of prayer), and he
leads them in the second rak’ah, then the imam (of prayer) sits, and they (the second
group) stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them, and they depart
with one taslimah.”
Imam {a.s} said: “And in Maghrib, it is similar to that; the imam (of prayer) stands, and a
group comes and stands behind him, and he leads them in prayer. Then he stands and
they stand, and the imam (of prayer) remains standing, and they pray two rak’ahs, then
recite the tashahhud and give salam to one another. Then they depart and go to the
position of their companions, and the others come and take the place of their
companions behind the imam (of prayer). Then he prays one rak’ah with them, reciting
in it, then he sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and they stand with him,
and he prays with them another rak’ah. Then he sits, and they stand and pray another
rak’ah, then he gives salam to them.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.455 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.171 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.1 p.455 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1063 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.1 p.494 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.436 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.544 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.3 p.527

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ مُحَمِّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ
أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلّى رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِأَصْحَابِهِ فِي غَزَاةِ ذَاتٍ
الرِّقَاعِ صَلَاةَ الْخَوْفِ فَفَرّقَ أَصْحَابَهُ فِرْقَتَيْنِ أَقَامَ فِرْقَةً بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوِّ وَ فِرْقَةً خَلْفَهُ فَكَبَّرَ وَ كَبَّرُوا فَقَرَأَ وَ أَنْصَثُوا
فَرَكَعَ وَ رَكَعُوا وَ سَجَدَ فَسَجَدُوا ثُمَّ اِسْتَتَمَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَائِماً وَ صَلَّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةَ ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ
بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ أَقَامُوا بِإِزَاءِ الْعَدُوِّ وَ جَاءَ أَصْحَابُهُمْ فَقَامُوا خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى
اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَصَلّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ تَشَهْدَ وَ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَامُوا فَصَلُّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةً وَ سَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ».
english_text:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam,
from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him.
Imam al-Sadiq {a.s} said: “The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his
family, prayed the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) with his companions in the
expedition of Dhat al-Riqa.
Prophet {saws} divided his companions into two groups;
He {saws} placed one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind him. He {saws}
said the takbir, and they said the takbir, then He {saws} recited and they listened.
Then He {saws} bowed and they bowed, and He {saws} prostrated and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, stood
upright, and they completed one rak’ah for themselves.
Then some of them gave salam to others, then they went to their companions and
stood facing the enemy,
And their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, may Allah
{SWT} bless him and his family. Then Prophet {saws} prayed one rak’ah with them, then
recited the tashahhud and gave salam to them. Then they stood and completed one
rak’ah for themselves and gave salam to one another.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s} & Abu al-Qasim Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah {saws}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.456 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.172 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1064 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.1 p.494 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.544 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.3 p.527

arabic_text:
الْحُسَيْنُ بْنْ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي
أَرْضِ مَخَافَةٍ فَخَشِيتَ لِصَّا أَوْ سَبُعاً فَصَلِّ الْفَرِيضَةَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى دَابَّتِكَ».
english_text:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Hammad from Abu Basir. He said:
I heard Abu Abdillah {a.s} say: “If you are in a land of fear and you fear a thief or a wild
beast, then pray the obligatory prayer while you are on your mount.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Al-Kafi, Vol.3 p.456 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.1 p.465 • Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.172 • Tafsir Al-Safi, Vol.1 p.269 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.239 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.2 p.370

arabic_text:
وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَخَافُ
مِنْ سَبُعٍ أَوْ لِضِّ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ «يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ».
english_text:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah {a.s}, peace be upon him, about a man who fears a wild beast or a
thief, how should he pray?
Imam {a.s} said: “He should say the takbir and gesture with his head.”
source: Abu Abdillah Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq {a.s}
references: Tahdib Al-Ahkam, Vol.3 p.173 • Al-Wafi, Vol.8 p.1072 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.8 p.442

arabic_text:
سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ
عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السّلاَمُ: «الَّذِي يَخَافُ اللَصُوصَ وَ السّبُعَ يُصَلِّي
صَلاةَ الْمُوَاقَفَةِ إِيمَاءً عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أْرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلْمُوَاقِفُ عَلَى وُضُوءِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ وَ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى
النْزُولِ قَالَ «يَتَيَمَّمُ مِنْ لِبْدِ سَرْجِهِ أَوْ دَابَّتِهِ أَوْ مِنْ مَعْرَفَةِ دَابَّتِهِ فَإِنَّ فِيهَا غُبَاراً وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يَجْعَلُ السَّجُودَ أَخْفَضَ
مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ لَا يَدُورُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ وَ لَكِنْ أَيْنَمَا دَارَتْ دَابَّتُهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يَسْتَقْبِلُ الْقِبْلَةَ بِأَوَّلِ تَكْبِيرَةِ جِينَ يَتَوَجَّهُ».
١٣ - باب صلاة المطاردة والمسايفة
english_text:
Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn
ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah. He said:
Abu Ja’far {a.s}, peace be upon him, said: “The one who fears thieves and wild beasts
should perform the prayer of those in dangerous situations, by gesturing while on his
mount.”
I (Zurarah) asked: “What if the person in such a situation, is not in a state of ablution
and is unable to dismount, what should he do?”
Imam {a.s} said: “He performs tayammum from the felt of his saddle or from his mount
or from the mane of his mount, for there is dust in it, and he performs the prayer, and
makes his prostration lower than his bowing.
He does not turn toward the qibla, but rather wherever his mount turns except that he
must face the qibla for the first takbirah when he begins the prayer.”
